title: Levin's decapitated flatworms keep their memories

tellings.quote: he trained these flat worms to respond to particular stimuli that he could measure their response they learned the effect then he cut their heads off

related.note: This is the same flatworm memory experiment as #9, but it puts forward morphic resonance in place of the conventional explanation.

plain: The biologist Michael Levin at Tufts University trained flatworms to respond to particular stimuli, then cut their heads off, and the worms that regrew are said to have kept what they had learned. The biologist Rupert Sheldrake describes the experiment to Michels as something he knows of, without naming a paper. It matters to him because it would mean memory is not stored only in the brain.
